clue.text: Gymnast may use this transport route across river

indicators.note: the transport route stretches across the river, so the river's letters sit inside it

parts.note: a tramline is the track a tram runs along
the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: Directions for a gymnast heading to training: take the tram line over the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gymnast may use this' is the definition, though it reads like the start of a sentence about travel; 'across' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast bounces on this sprung canvas frame to perform aerial routines.

clue.text: Call American combine that has banks in European capital

definitions.text: that has banks in European capital

parts.note: to tag is to label or call

explanation.surface: A US conglomerate with banking interests in a European capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' are riverbanks, not financial houses: the river flows through Lisbon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tagus is the river that flows through Lisbon, Portugal's capital.

clue.text: Promise conviction

definitions.meaning: a pledge or guarantee
firm certainty or confidence

explanation.definitionFit: A pledge given, and a feeling of confident certainty.

clue.text: Sensible card for one playing trick

parts.note: practical means sensible, down to earth
the joker is a card in the pack

explanation.surface: A level-headed card player pulls off a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A prankster plays pranks on people.

clue.text: Tedious dance? Certainly not a wonderful ball!

parts.note: long can mean wearisome, dragging
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A dull dance is far from a splendid ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a long hop is a short-pitched, easily hit delivery; 'ball' looks like a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket delivery pitched so short it is easy to hit, a poor bowl.

clue.text: Person uninvolved in fight is not charged

definitions.meaning: someone or a state that takes no side in a war
having no electric charge

explanation.surface: A bystander in a brawl faces no charges.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-combatant takes no side; in physics the word means bearing no electric charge.

clue.text: Deceiver abandoning daughter and wife in Europe

indicators.note: the deceiver walks away from the daughter, so her letter leaves the word

parts.note: a fraud is a cheat or impostor

explanation.surface: A con man deserts his daughter and his wife somewhere on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' removes D from FRAUD.
explanation.definitionFit: German for a married woman or wife, used as the title Mrs.

clue.text: Type of major road intersection?

parts.note: a style of upright typeface shares its name with the people whose straight highways crossed Europe, and whose numeral for ten looks like a crossing

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of junction a motorway has.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' is a printing typeface; the X of a crossroads is a numeral of the same people.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright type, as opposed to italic, is named after the ancient Latin people who built major roads.

clue.text: Sneaky way to make deliveries

definitions.meaning: secret and deceitful
bowling or throwing with the hand below the shoulder

explanation.surface: A crafty method of getting parcels delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliveries' are bowled balls, not parcels.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceitful, and a style of bowling with the hand kept low.

clue.text: Does it stir no alien man, that?

definitions.text: Does it stir no alien man, that?

indicators.note: stir means mix, so the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A question whether a patriotic song moves only natives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' mixes NO ALIEN MAN THAT; the whole clue also describes the song.
explanation.definitionFit: A country's official song is meant to rouse its own citizens, not foreigners.

clue.text: Profit out of a manuscript put back in pipeline

indicators.note: the profit is placed outside, so the other letters come out of its middle

parts.note: gain means profit

indicators.note: the words a manuscript are written backwards

explanation.surface: Someone makes money from an old manuscript and returns it to a pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' gives SMA; 'out of' reads as the profit going round it, though it looks like a source.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas main is the large underground pipe carrying the supply along a street.

clue.text: Not 'urt in this form of combat

definitions.meaning: safe and unhurt, said with the H dropped as a Cockney would, the apostrophe marking the lost letter
fighting with bare hands and no weapons, as in the phrase for that kind of combat

explanation.surface: A Cockney fighter boasts he came through the bout without a scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the H from UNHARMED, as the apostrophe in 'urt invites.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhurt is unharmed; the H-less spelling also describes combat without weapons.

clue.text: Rack that's provided for case when travelling

definitions.meaning: a frame on which something is stretched, as a rack stretched its victims
a casualty, the medical 'case', is carried on one when moved

explanation.surface: A luggage rack is supplied for a suitcase on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' means a patient, not luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretcher is a frame for stretching things, and a litter for carrying the injured.

clue.text: Private accommodation used by monarch

parts.note: an inn provides lodging for travellers
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Private rooms set aside for the use of the sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts are private ones, kept within.

clue.text: Lose bottle in the grass

definitions.meaning: British slang for losing one's nerve
a genus of grasses, including millet, shares the name

explanation.surface: Someone loses their bottle somewhere in the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose bottle' is British slang for losing courage, not misplacing a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose one's nerve is to be gripped by fear; a millet-type plant also bears the name.

clue.text: Corrupt coper with tip about horse, providing forecast

indicators.note: the scrambled words go about, around, the horse
corrupt means spoiled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: H is slang for heroin, which is known as horse

explanation.surface: A crooked horse dealer passes on a racing tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' gives PROPETIC; 'about' wraps that round the horse. A coper is a horse dealer, which makes the surface a racing scam.
explanation.definitionFit: Prophetic means foretelling the future.

clue.text: Where you'll find quiet, with only sea and island resort

definitions.text: Where you'll find quiet, with only sea and island resort

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A holiday blurb promises peace, nothing but sea and islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' is read as re-sort, making OLYNESIA; it looks like a holiday destination.
explanation.definitionFit: This Pacific region is a scatter of islands across open ocean, a tranquil getaway.

clue.text: What slaves performed is immaterial

definitions.meaning: a religious folk song of enslaved Africans in America
of the spirit, not physical

explanation.surface: What slaves did is irrelevant.
explanation.definitionFit: A gospel song sung on plantations, and an adjective for things of the soul.

clue.text: Some cricket at test ground for top people

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls in cricket
Lord's is the London cricket ground that hosts Test matches

explanation.surface: Watching part of a Test match at the ground in the company of the elite.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD'S is a London cricket ground; an over is six deliveries from one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlords are rulers placed above everyone else.

clue.text: Stand up on vessel for portrait painter

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to bear is to stand or tolerate
an urn is a vase-like vessel

explanation.surface: A painter has his portrait propped on a vase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns BEAR into RAEB. Henry Raeburn was a Scottish portrait painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Henry Raeburn painted portraits of Edinburgh society.

clue.text: Big noise made by revolting Euro- MP's

indicators.note: the members are in revolt, so the letters turn over into a new order

parts.note: the letters of Euro and MPs

explanation.surface: Rebellious Euro-MPs make a lot of noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' rearranges EUROMPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the person in charge, an important figure.

clue.text: Taking part in special airdrop, he's landed in Scotland

indicators.note: Taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A paratrooper joins a special drop and comes down in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landed' means owning land, not touching down.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish landowner holds an estate, so he is a landed proprietor.

clue.text: Ancient city where physician loses crates, finally

indicators.note: the physician gives up the crates, so those letters are taken from his name

parts.note: Hippocrates was the ancient Greek father of medicine
taken as written

explanation.surface: In an old city a doctor loses his boxes at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' notes the crates come off the end of the name. Hippo was a North African city, St Augustine's see.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippo Regius was a Roman-era port in present-day Algeria.

clue.text: Chairman conceals nothing in demonstration

indicators.note: the chairman hides the letter inside

parts.note: a professor holds a chair at a university
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A committee chair hides that nothing was shown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chairman' is a professor, holder of a university chair.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof is evidence that demonstrates something is true.

clue.text: Wide river entered by vessels. I see

indicators.note: the river is entered, so the other letters go inside it

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
pans are cooking vessels
v stands for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: A broad river where boats sail in, as someone observes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entered by' signals the container; the Exe is a Devon river, and V for vide (see) is a convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Expansive means extending over a large area, broad.

clue.text: Those competing for the record

definitions.meaning: the field of entrants in a competition
an item written in a log or register

explanation.surface: Athletes in a race, for the record.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of entrants, and an item noted in a register.

clue.text: English author upset American one

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A British writer is offended by an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges E and AUTHOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry David Thoreau, of Walden fame, was an American writer.

clue.text: One's found behind car, run down

definitions.meaning: the pipe at the rear of a vehicle
worn out, tired

explanation.surface: Someone discovered behind a car, worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: The tailpipe of a vehicle, and a verb meaning to tire out completely.

clue.text: Strike end of arm

definitions.meaning: to hit with an open hand
the band at the wrist end of a sleeve

explanation.surface: A blow struck with the end of one's arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A light blow, and the turned band at the wrist end of a sleeve.

clue.text: Advise to get married without ceremony

parts.note: to inform is to tell or advise
to ally is to unite, as by marriage

explanation.surface: Telling someone to wed with no fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally means casually, with no formality.
